title: Sales order to production order
text:
# Sales order to production order

Scenario: ERP/MES integration
Source type: SOP
Tags: ERP, MES, sales order, production order

A sales order records customer demand. A production order converts confirmed demand into a manufacturing execution plan. In an ERP-MES integration, the ERP system usually owns customer demand, pricing, and delivery commitment, while MES owns shop-floor execution, reporting, and exception feedback.

title: BOM version change handling
text:
# BOM version change handling

Scenario: BOM/MRP
Source type: Implementation note
Tags: BOM, MRP, engineering change

When a BOM version changes, the team should confirm the effective date, affected sales orders, open production orders, and existing inventory. If a work order has already started, the system should avoid silent replacement and create an exception review task.

title: Inventory inconsistency between WMS and MES
text:
# Inventory inconsistency between WMS and MES

Scenario: WMS/MES exception
Source type: Exception playbook
Tags: WMS, MES, inventory, material consumption

If WMS inventory differs from MES material consumption, the assistant should ask for material code, warehouse, batch number, work order, and transaction time. Typical causes include delayed posting, manual adjustment, barcode scanning error, or cross-warehouse transfer not synchronized.

title: Quality inspection exception escalation
text:
# Quality inspection exception escalation

Scenario: Quality management
Source type: SOP
Tags: QC, inspection, nonconformance

When inspection fails, the system should record defect category, defect quantity, responsible process, inspector, photos if available, and disposition decision. The next step may be rework, concession release, scrap, or supplier claim.

title: Manufacturing gross margin analysis
text:
# Manufacturing gross margin analysis

Scenario: Finance analysis
Source type: Analysis template
Tags: finance, cost, gross margin

Manufacturing gross margin analysis should compare sales revenue, material cost, labor cost, manufacturing overhead, outsourcing cost, and abnormal loss. The assistant should separate order-level margin from product-line margin and highlight data source assumptions.
